slides.title: SocietyBench: Forecasting Counterfactual Social-World Evolution
slides.highlight: SocietyBench evaluates the ability of LLM agents to forecast social events using counterfactual timelines, supporting MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and impact analysis.

card.one_liner: SocietyBench evaluates LLM forecasting of real social events using anonymized, counterfactual timelines to prevent memory-based recall.
card.key_idea: Real events are transformed into counterfactual worlds via entity substitution and date shifting, then scored on probability calibration and temporal accuracy across dual-source (news/social media) timelines.
card.evaluation: Six frontier LLMs, three agent frameworks, and two heuristics were tested on five heterogeneous events. GPT-5.5 led with a 75.0/100 score.
card.limitation: High per-event score variance (up to 21.4 points) makes single-event evaluations unreliable for comparing model performance.

slides.title: No One Wins in Nuclear War: A Social Simulation of Military Decision-making
slides.highlight: WOPR provides a verifiable rules engine and collective command-and-control systems for simulating high-stakes organizational decisions, supporting the societal-scale simulation goals of MIMIC.

card.one_liner: WOPR is a social-simulation environment for studying high-stakes organizational decision-making via a verifiable rules engine.
card.key_idea: A deterministic, replay-validated engine using a decision-point contract, a four-rung communication 'press ladder', and four distinct command-and-control archetypes for collective faction decision-making.
card.evaluation: Verified via a 240-game sweep confirming seeded outcomes are preserved; instantiated using the card game 'Nuclear War' with a rule conformance matrix.
card.limitation: Early-stage work; lacks controlled studies across communication rungs and only provides a worked example for the council archetype.

slides.title: Designing Social Robots for Inclusive Child Wellbeing Assessment: Insights from Communities Supporting Developmental Language Disorder and Forced Migration
slides.highlight: This research provides design recommendations for using social robots to assess the wellbeing of children with communication barriers, supporting the RwB focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Design guidance for inclusive social robot-mediated wellbeing assessments for children with communication barriers and forced migration backgrounds.
card.key_idea: Used design probes and focus groups with parents and professionals to identify ethical and inclusive requirements for robot-led activities targeting language, social, and emotional indicators.
card.evaluation: Thematic analysis of focus group discussions with 14 stakeholders (parents and professionals) across DLD and forced migration contexts.
card.limitation: The study relies on stakeholder perspectives rather than direct interaction data from the children themselves.

slides.title: Hybrid Attention Estimation Pipeline for Adaptive HRI Using an Expressive Robotic Head
slides.tldr: HYBRID ATTENTION ESTIMATION FOR ADAPTIVE HRI
slides.highlight: This work proposes a pipeline combining geometric and semantic perception to regulate adaptive interaction behaviors in an expressive robotic head, contributing to the development of embodied social robots for RwB.

card.one_liner: A hybrid attention pipeline for an expressive robotic head that adapts interaction based on user distraction.
card.key_idea: Combines a fast geometric layer (MediaPipe head-pose) for real-time state regulation with a VLM-based semantic layer (LLaVA-Phi3) for contextual interpretation via a finite state machine.
card.evaluation: Tested with 10 participants (40 trials); showed reliable interaction starts and successful adaptive pausing/resuming in distraction scenarios.
card.limitation: Controlled experimental setup, small participant sample, and lack of manual frame-level ground truth for attention labels.

slides.title: Dobot Launches Full-Scenario Embodied Humanoid Robot
slides.highlight: Dobot has introduced a multi-functional smart companion humanoid robot designed for daily and professional needs, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: Humanoid Companion Robot Market Projected to Reach US$1.1bn by 2030
slides.tldr: GROWTH IN HUMANOID COMPANION ROBOT MARKET
slides.highlight: The increasing demand for caregiving and emotional support is driving market growth for humanoid companion robots. This trend aligns with RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

slides.title: TIDES: A Longitudinal Bilingual Dataset for Modeling Multi-Party Social Dynamics
slides.tldr: LONGITUDINAL DATASET FOR MULTI-PARTY SOCIAL DYNAMICS
slides.highlight: TIDES provides a longitudinal dataset of in-person meetings with annotations on interaction types and emergent roles, supporting HyECHO's focus on modeling hybrid team states and group norms.

card.one_liner: TIDES is a longitudinal bilingual dataset of university project teams used to model multi-party social dynamics.
card.key_idea: A dataset of 75,971 utterances with socio-structural annotations (interaction types, emergent roles, development stages) to improve LLM next-speaker prediction and structural understanding in group conversations.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via next-speaker/intention prediction and generation tasks. Fine-tuning improved speaker prediction by 13.8pp over bigram baseline and performed competitively on the AMI Meeting Corpus.
card.limitation: Improved structural prediction (next-speaker) does not necessarily translate to more natural or coherent utterance generation according to human evaluations.

slides.title: When AI Joins the Team! A Model of How AI Adoption Relates To Social Patterns in Software Engineering Teams
slides.tldr: AI ADOPTION AND TEAM SOCIAL DYNAMICS
slides.highlight: This research examines how AI tools influence social patterns and communication quality in software teams, contributing to HyECHO's focus on understanding the state of hybrid human-AI team engagement.

card.one_liner: AI adoption reduces community smells through distinct mechanisms depending on whether work involves specialization or coordination.
card.key_idea: Using Transactive Memory Systems theory and PLS-SEM, the study models AI's impact on social anti-patterns via specialization-oriented and coordination-oriented human-human interactions.
card.evaluation: Tested five PLS-SEM models using survey data from 152 software professionals; constructs were validated via expert surveys and Exploratory Factor Analysis.
card.limitation: The expert validation panel for cluster structure was small, consisting of only four senior researchers.

slides.title: Deep Learning for Real-Time Sound Order Recognition in Human-Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: REAL-TIME SOUND ORDER RECOGNITION FOR HRI
slides.highlight: This research proposes a deep learning framework to recognize the temporal order of overlapping sounds, which is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A deep learning framework for real-time recognition of the temporal order of overlapping non-verbal sounds.
card.key_idea: A multi-branch CNN processing Mel spectrograms, MFCCs, and STFT features, utilizing an attention-based fusion mechanism to identify sound sequences.
card.evaluation: Tested on synthetic overlaps (balanced, varied-amplitude, and unseen sounds); achieved 99% accuracy for balanced and 74% for unseen data.
card.limitation: Experiments relied on carefully controlled synthetic overlaps, raising concerns regarding ecological validity in real-room environments.

slides.title: Neuro-Symbolic Participation Governance for Verifiable AI Agents in Open Digital Twin Ecosystems
slides.tldr: NEURO-SYMBOLIC GOVERNANCE FOR VERIFIABLE AI AGENTS
slides.highlight: This work proposes a neuro-symbolic decentralized governance framework to ensure policy compliance and verifiable identity for AI agents, supporting the societal-scale simulation and agent modeling goals of MIMIC.

card.one_liner: A decentralized governance framework using neuro-symbolic profiles and blockchain to verify AI agent capabilities and compliance.
card.key_idea: Binds LLM agents to symbolic domain ontologies via Verifiable Credentials, using blockchain smart contracts for identity verification, dynamic role binding, and immutable interaction logging.
card.evaluation: Tested with 42 cases (security, policy, scalability) using a healthcare prototype; achieved 100% attack detection and O(1) verification complexity.
card.limitation: Focuses on admission governance and provenance; does not verify the actual quality or correctness of the agent's clinical recommendations.

slides.title: Toward Resilient Human-AI Collaboration: A Lifecycle Taxonomy of Sociotechnical Risks and Cascading Failures
slides.tldr: SOCIOTECHNICAL RISK TAXONOMY FOR HUMAN-AI COLLABORATION
slides.highlight: This work identifies recurring risk clusters and cascading failures in human-AI collaboration, providing a framework for understanding the sociotechnical dynamics relevant to HyECHO's focus on hybrid team states.

card.one_liner: A lifecycle taxonomy identifying six recurring sociotechnical risk clusters that undermine resilient human-AI collaboration across diverse domains.
card.key_idea: A framework mapping risks across four stages (task allocation, interaction, feedback, adoption) and clustering them into trust, cognitive, accountability, capability, goal, and psychological risks.
card.evaluation: Synthesized evidence from fragmented literature across five domains (healthcare, journalism, education, management, defense) to identify cross-domain failure patterns.
card.limitation: The work provides a conceptual interaction model and taxonomy for future empirical validation rather than new experimental data.

slides.title: Robot Learning from Human Demonstrations: Handwritten Alphabet Trajectories and Human-Likeness Evaluation
slides.tldr: LEARNING HUMAN-LIKE ROBOT MOTION FROM HANDWRITING DEMONSTRATIONS
slides.highlight: This work proposes a framework for learning human-like robot motion from handwriting demonstrations, which is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied learning.

card.one_liner: A framework for learning human-like robot handwriting using an extended GMM+GMR approach and a new dataset.
card.key_idea: Extends GMM+GMR by incorporating contact force and normalized time dimensions and implementing segment-wise processing to handle non-continuous, multi-stroke trajectories.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via a user study (21 participants) on 52 character-case combinations; achieved a mean human-likeness score of 71.50/100.
card.limitation: Used simulated robots instead of physical systems; small participant samples; linear interpolation for pen-lift transitions; no pen orientation data.

slides.title: Accelerating Human-Aware Robot Trajectory Generation via Diffusion and Consistency Distillation
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework for generating safe, collision-aware robot trajectories in HRI environments using diffusion and consistency distillation. It is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied AI.

card.one_liner: Accelerates human-aware robot trajectory generation using a consistency-distilled diffusion model with joint-weighted jerk regularization.
card.key_idea: A conditional diffusion model trained on RRT/RRT* data is distilled into a consistency model for fast inference, utilizing constraint-guided sampling and a jerk-penalizing loss function.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via UR5 simulations (500 test scenes); consistency models generated 150 candidates in <100ms with high success rates and reduced jerk.
card.limitation: The study was validated only in simulation using a UR5 manipulator; real-world physical deployment is not clearly stated.

slides.title: PromptShield Home: Ambient Multimodal Prompt Injection Defense for Smart-Home Agents
slides.tldr: MULTIMODAL PROMPT INJECTION DEFENSE FOR SMART-HOME AGENTS
slides.highlight: This work introduces a benchmark for smart-home agents to distinguish genuine user commands from ambient multimodal content, relating to HyECHO's focus on addressee modeling and social perception.

card.one_liner: PromptShield-Home benchmarks multimodal prompt injection in smart homes, finding MLLMs over-refuse while traditional detectors over-execute.
card.key_idea: A comparative framework testing three layers: traditional detectors (L0), single MLLM agents (L1), and multi-agent mediation (L2) to distinguish genuine commands from ambient noise.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on a 19-scenario pilot benchmark using unsafe-execution and safe-completion rates. Results show complementary failure modes between L0 and MLLMs.
card.limitation: Small benchmark size (N=19), reliance on an oracle for complementarity results, and high VRAM requirements for the vision model.
